title: Plane Figures
html:
A plane figure is a flat shape: a triangle, a quadrilateral, a polygon, a circle. Geometry at this level is mostly bookkeeping with two facts — the angles of a triangle add to 180°, and the angles of a polygon follow from splitting it into triangles. Everything else is a consequence, and the figures are what make those consequences visible.

What this chapter asks of you

You should be able to classify triangles and quadrilaterals and state their properties, find the interior and exterior angles of a polygon, construct a triangle or a quadrilateral from given measurements, and use the vocabulary of the circle.

14.1 Triangles

A triangle is a closed figure with three sides and three angles. Its three interior angles always add to 180°, and any exterior angle equals the sum of the two interior opposite angles.

Classified by sides Property
Equilateral all three sides equal, all three angles 60°
Isosceles two sides equal, and the angles opposite them equal
Scalene no sides equal, no angles equal
Classified by angles Property
Acute-angled all three angles less than 90°
Right-angled one angle is 90°; the side opposite it is the hypotenuse
Obtuse-angled one angle more than 90°

Properties verified in class (by cutting, folding and measuring):

  • The three angles of any triangle add to 180° (tear off the corners and put them together: they make a straight angle).
  • All three angles of an equilateral triangle are equal, so each is 180°\div3=60°.
  • The base angles of an isosceles triangle (the angles opposite the equal sides) are equal.
  • In a right-angled isosceles triangle each base angle is \frac{180°-90°}{2}=45°.
Angles of a triangle

Problem. In a triangle the angles are in the ratio 2:3:4. Find each angle and classify the triangle.

Solution. Let the angles be 2x, 3x and 4x. Their sum is 180°:

2x+3x+4x=180\;\Longrightarrow\;9x=180\;\Longrightarrow\;x=20

The angles are 40°, 60° and 80°. All three are less than 90°, so the triangle is acute-angled.

Check. 40+60+80=180 ✓, and the ratios 40:60:80=2:3:4 ✓.

Isosceles triangle

Problem. In an isosceles triangle the vertex angle is 40°. Find the base angles.

Solution. The two base angles are equal; let each be x. Then

40+x+x=180\;\Longrightarrow\;2x=140\;\Longrightarrow\;x=70

Answer. Each base angle is 70°.

Check. 40+70+70=180 ✓. The vertex angle is the odd one out, and the two angles opposite the equal sides are equal.

14.2 Quadrilaterals

A quadrilateral has four sides and four angles, and its angles add to 360°.

Quadrilateral Sides Angles Diagonals
Parallelogram both pairs of opposite sides parallel and equal opposite angles equal; adjacent angles supplementary bisect each other
Rectangle parallelogram with a right angle all four angles 90° equal and bisect each other
Square rectangle with all sides equal all four angles 90° equal, bisect at right angles
Rhombus parallelogram with all sides equal opposite angles equal bisect each other at right angles
Trapezium exactly one pair of opposite sides parallel angles on the same side of a leg supplementary —
Kite two pairs of adjacent equal sides one pair of opposite angles equal cross at right angles

Diagonal properties to remember.

  • Rhombus: the diagonals bisect each other at right angles, and each diagonal bisects the angles at its ends.
  • Kite: the diagonals cut at right angles; the longer diagonal bisects the shorter one (the shorter is not bisected by the longer).
  • Trapezium: only one pair of opposite sides is parallel, so a trapezium is not a parallelogram. In an isosceles trapezium the non-parallel sides are equal.
  • Every square is a rhombus, but not every rhombus is a square.
Using the rhombus diagonals

Problem. The diagonals of rhombus PQRS meet at O. If ∠PQO =35°, find ∠POQ, ∠QPO and ∠PQR.

Solution. ∠POQ =90° (diagonals of a rhombus cut at right angles). In \triangle POQ: ∠QPO =180°-90°-35°=55°. ∠PQR =2\times∠PQO =70° (the diagonal QS bisects ∠PQR).

Angles of a quadrilateral

Problem. Three angles of a quadrilateral are 85°, 95° and 110°. Find the fourth.

Solution. The four angles add to 360°, so the fourth is

360-(85+95+110)=360-290=70°

Answer. 70°.

Check. 85+95+110+70=360 ✓.

Properties of a parallelogram

Problem. In a parallelogram, one angle is 65°. Find the other three and state the property you used each time.

Solution. The opposite angle is 65° (opposite angles of a parallelogram are equal). Each of the other two is the supplement: 180-65=115° (adjacent angles of a parallelogram are supplementary), and they are equal to each other by the opposite-angle property.

Answer. 65°, 115°, 115°.

Check. 65+115+65+115=360 ✓.

14.3 Polygons

A polygon is a closed plane figure bounded by straight sides. A polygon is regular when all its sides and all its angles are equal.

For a polygon with n sides:

\text{sum of interior angles}=(n-2)\times180°

\text{each interior angle of a regular polygon}=\frac{(n-2)\times180°}{n}

\text{sum of exterior angles}=360°\qquad\text{(always, for every polygon)}

\text{each exterior angle of a regular polygon}=\frac{360°}{n}

The first formula comes from splitting the polygon into triangles by drawing all the diagonals from one vertex: an n-sided polygon gives n-2 triangles.

Polygon Sides n Sum of interior angles Each angle (regular)
Triangle 3 180° 60°
Quadrilateral 4 360° 90°
Pentagon 5 540° 108°
Hexagon 6 720° 120°
Octagon 8 1080° 135°
Decagon 10 1440° 144°
Interior and exterior angles

Problem. Each exterior angle of a regular polygon is 24°. Find the number of sides, the sum of the interior angles, and each interior angle.

Solution. The exterior angles add to 360°, so

n=\frac{360}{24}=15

Sum of interior angles: (15-2)\times180=13\times180=2340°.

Each interior angle: \frac{2340}{15}=156°, or equivalently 180-24=156°.

Answer. 15 sides; 2340°; 156°.

Check. 156+24=180 ✓ — an interior and its exterior angle form a linear pair.

Finding the number of sides

Problem. The sum of the interior angles of a polygon is 1260°. Find the number of sides.

Solution. (n-2)\times180=1260, so n-2=7 and n=9.

Answer. A nonagon, with 9 sides.

Check. (9-2)\times180=1260 ✓.

Exterior angles are not supplementary to each other

A polygon has one exterior angle at each vertex, and those n angles add to 360° for every polygon, regular or not. The fact that an interior angle and its own exterior angle add to 180° is a separate statement about the same vertex. Do not confuse the two.

14.4 Construction

Constructions are done with a ruler and a pair of compasses, and every line must be drawn, not estimated.

To construct Given Method
A triangle three sides (SSS) draw one side, then arcs of the other two lengths from its ends
A triangle two sides and the included angle (SAS) draw the included angle with a protractor or compasses, then mark off both sides
A triangle two angles and a side (ASA) draw the side, then the two angles at its ends
A quadrilateral four sides and one diagonal draw the diagonal, then construct the two triangles on either side
A right angle — bisect a straight angle with compasses
Four habits that earn the construction marks

(1) Draw the given side first and label it with its length. (2) Keep the compass opening unchanged while striking a pair of arcs. (3) Draw arcs long enough to cross clearly — a faint arc gives a faint intersection. (4) Mark every given measurement on the figure and leave all construction arcs in place; an erased construction loses the method marks even if the figure is right.

14.4.1 Constructing a rectangle and a parallelogram

The Grade 8 textbook asks for these constructions (ruler, compasses and protractor). Always draw a rough sketch with the measurements first.

Rectangle ABCD with AB = 6 cm, AD = 4 cm. 1. Draw AB = 6 cm. 2. At A and at B construct angles of 90°. 3. Cut AD = 4 cm and BC = 4 cm on these lines. 4. Join DC. Check: DC should measure 6 cm.

Parallelogram — three cases. (Opposite sides of a parallelogram are equal, so after drawing two adjacent sides the fourth vertex is found with two arcs.)

Given Steps
two adjacent sides and the included angle (AB = 5 cm, BC = 4 cm, ∠B = 60°) draw BC; make 60° at B; cut BA = 5 cm; from A arc 4 cm, from C arc 5 cm; they meet at D
two adjacent sides and a diagonal (AB = 5 cm, BC = 4 cm, AC = 6 cm) draw AC; from A arc 5 cm and from C arc 4 cm to get B; then from A arc 4 cm and from C arc 5 cm on the other side to get D
a side, a diagonal and the angle between them draw the side, make the angle, cut the diagonal on it; complete with two arcs as above

14.5 The circle

Term Meaning
Centre the fixed point inside the circle
Radius the distance from the centre to any point on the circle
Chord a line segment joining two points on the circle
Diameter a chord through the centre, equal to 2r
Arc a part of the circle's boundary
Sector the region between two radii and an arc
Segment the region between a chord and an arc
Circumference the whole distance round the circle, 2\pi r

Results worth knowing.

  • A diameter is the longest chord.
  • A perpendicular from the centre to a chord bisects the chord.
  • Equal chords are at equal distances from the centre.
  • The angle in a semicircle is a right angle.
A chord and the centre

Problem. A chord of length 16 cm is drawn in a circle of radius 10 cm. Find the distance of the chord from the centre.

Solution. The perpendicular from the centre bisects the chord, so half the chord is 8 cm. That, the radius and the distance d form a right triangle with the radius as the hypotenuse:

d=\sqrt{10^2-8^2}=\sqrt{100-64}=\sqrt{36}=6\ \text{cm}

Answer. 6 cm from the centre.

Check. \sqrt{6^2+8^2}=\sqrt{36+64}=10 ✓, which is the radius.

Chapter summary

  • The angles of a triangle add to 180°; an exterior angle equals the sum of the two interior opposite angles.
  • Equilateral, isosceles and scalene are classified by sides; acute, right and obtuse by angles.
  • The angles of a quadrilateral add to 360°; a parallelogram has equal opposite angles and supplementary adjacent angles, and its diagonals bisect each other.
  • For a polygon of n sides: interior angles sum to (n-2)\times180°; exterior angles always sum to 360°.
  • The perpendicular from the centre to a chord bisects the chord; the angle in a semicircle is 90°.
  • Constructions are done with ruler and compasses, with every arc left in place.

Practice questions

Group A — Objective (1 mark each)

  1. The sum of the angles of a triangle is [1]a90°b180°c270°d360°
  2. An equilateral triangle has each angle equal to [1]a45°b60°c90°d120°
  3. The sum of the angles of a quadrilateral is [1]a180°b270°c360°d540°
  4. Each interior angle of a regular hexagon is [1]a60°b108°c120°d135°
  5. The sum of the exterior angles of any polygon is [1]a180°b360°c540°dn\times180°
  6. The longest chord of a circle is its [1]aradiusbarccdiameterdtangent
Answers to Group A

1. (b) — 180°.

2. (b) — 180\div3=60.

3. (c) — 360°.

4. (c) — \frac{(6-2)180}{6}=120.

5. (b) — 360° for every polygon.

6. (c) — the diameter passes through the centre.

Group B — Short answer (2 marks each)

  1. Two angles of a triangle are 55° and 65°. Find the third and say what kind of triangle it is. [2]
  2. Find the sum of the interior angles of a decagon. [2]
  3. In a parallelogram one angle is 72°. Find the other three angles. [2]
  4. A chord of length 24 cm is 5 cm from the centre of a circle. Find the radius. [2]
Answers to Group B

1. 180-(55+65)=60°; all angles are less than 90°, so it is acute-angled.

2. (10-2)\times180=1440°.

3. The opposite angle is 72° and the other two are each 180-72=108°.

4. Half the chord is 12 cm, so r=\sqrt{12^2+5^2}=\sqrt{169}=13 cm.

Group C — Long answer (4 marks each)

  1. Each interior angle of a regular polygon is 150°. Find the number of sides, each exterior angle, and the sum of the interior angles. [4]
  2. Construct a triangle ABC in which BC=6 cm, AB=4.5 cm and \angle B=60°. Measure AC and the other two angles, and check that the angles add to 180°. [4]
Answers to Group C

1. If each interior angle is 150°, each exterior angle is 180-150=30°. The exterior angles add to 360°, so n=\frac{360}{30}=12 sides. The sum of the interior angles is (12-2)\times180=1800°. Check. \frac{1800}{12}=150° ✓, which is the given interior angle, so the answer is consistent.

2. Construction. Draw BC=6 cm with a ruler. At B, construct an angle of 60° (an equilateral triangle on BC gives it exactly with compasses). With centre B and radius 4.5 cm, strike an arc on that ray; call the intersection A. Join AC. Measurements. AC\approx5.4 cm, \angle A\approx74° and \angle C\approx46°. Check. 60+74+46=180 ✓. The construction is the SAS case, and it always gives exactly one triangle, which is why the two measurements agree from any correct drawing. The side opposite the 60° angle is the one you were asked to measure, and it is the middle length, as it must be.

Extra practice — textbook-style questions

1. True or false? Correct the false ones. (a) All the angles of an isosceles triangle are equal. (b) All rhombuses are squares. (c) The diagonals of a rhombus bisect each other at right angles. (d) All trapeziums are parallelograms.

2. Find the sum of the interior angles and each interior angle of a regular octagon.

3. Find each exterior angle of a regular polygon with 9 sides.

4. Construct a rectangle PQRS with PQ = 7 cm and QR = 4 cm.

Extra practice — answers

1. (a) False — only the two base angles are equal. (b) False — all squares are rhombuses, not the other way round. (c) True. (d) False — a trapezium has only one pair of parallel sides.

2. Sum =(8-2)\times180°=1080°; each angle =\frac{1080°}{8}=135°.

3. \frac{360°}{9}=40°.

4. Draw PQ = 7 cm; make 90° at P and Q; cut PS = QR = 4 cm; join SR (it measures 7 cm).

Objective practice

Choose the correct answer. [5×1=5]

1. The sum of the interior angles of a quadrilateral is (a) 180° (b) 270° (c) 360° (d) 540°

2. Each interior angle of a regular pentagon is (a) 72° (b) 108° (c) 120° (d) 135°

3. A quadrilateral with all sides equal and no right angle is a (a) square (b) rhombus (c) rectangle (d) trapezium

4. The diagonals of a rectangle are (a) equal and bisect each other (b) perpendicular (c) unequal (d) parallel

5. The number of sides of a regular polygon whose exterior angle is 36° is (a) 8 (b) 9 (c) 10 (d) 12

Objective practice — answers

1. (c) — 360°.

2. (b) — \frac{(5-2)180°}{5} = 108°.

3. (b) — a rhombus.

4. (a) — equal and bisecting.

5. (c) — \frac{360°}{36°} = 10.
